abstract: Maintains membrane recovery ratings, fouling mitigation systems, and hydraulic flux verification logs
system_message:
You are Process engineering lead (ENG). The Process engineering lead (ENG) oversees process engineering evaluations, maintaining membrane recovery ratings, fouling mitigation systems, and hydraulic flux verification logs, as well as chemical reagent sourcing specifications for candidate reverse osmosis expansion consortia.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Chemical reagent sourcing（CHEM）
information_points.content:
ENG-CHEM-YTV：Pacific Desalination Solutions allocates a coagulant bulk storage capacity of 15 m3 for liquid ferric chloride storage in the pretreatment chemical dosing building.
ENG-CHEM-F2V：HydroVentures Engineering Group provides a coagulant bulk storage capacity of 35 m3 for liquid ferric chloride within its pretreatment chemical dosing facility.
ENG-CHEM-32I：According to the pretreatment chemical dosing building design sheet, Aquatech Infrastructure Partners provides a coagulant bulk storage capacity of 25 m3 dedicated to liquid ferric chloride.

information_points.title: Maintains membrane recovery ratings, fouling mitigation systems, and hydraulic flux verification logs（PROC）
information_points.content:
ENG-PROC-Q11：HydroVentures Engineering Group maintains an active antiscalant fouling mitigation system on its primary reverse osmosis rack. Testing under steady-state conditions at nominal feed salinity records a membrane permeate recovery rate of 72 %, alongside a validated membrane permeate flux rate of 250 m3/h for its first-pass train.
ENG-PROC-NXI：Aquatech Infrastructure Partners has active antiscalant fouling mitigation verified on its primary reverse osmosis rack per the process flow diagram and dosing specification. Under continuous steady-state operation at nominal feed salinity, its membrane permeate recovery rate is 75 %, and its validated membrane permeate flux rate for the first-pass reverse osmosis train is certified at 350 m3/h at nominal transmembrane pressure.
ENG-PROC-J7E：Pacific Desalination Solutions features an active antiscalant fouling mitigation system on its primary reverse osmosis rack. In continuous steady-state operation at nominal feed salinity, it achieves a membrane permeate recovery rate of 82 %, with a validated membrane permeate flux rate of 300 m3/h at nominal transmembrane pressure.
